subject: Proposed strict routing for FinBank: region lock + no-fallback + model constraint
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Customer ask: FinBank requires strict routing

Hi team,

FinBank sent over a requirements spreadsheet this morning (attached). They need a strict routing configuration for production: all inference traffic for their account must terminate in the eu-west region, with no automatic fallback to other regions or to lower-tier model variants. They also want the ability to pin to a specific model revision (they called this out as "model lock") and to prevent any transparent substitution (no quantized fallback allowed without explicit approval).

Key points from Marcus at FinBank:
- Region: eu-west only (data residency)
- No automatic fallbacks: if eu-west capacity is constrained, requests should fail fast and return a 503 rather than being routed elsewhere
- Forced model selection: customer will specify a model hash/revision; runtime must guarantee that exact model artifact serves requests for their tenant

Ask: is this feasible from infra/ops perspective and what are the product/contract implications? I included the requirement matrix and a first-pass routing policy (proposed-routing-policy.yaml).

Timeline: Sales is targeting a pilot start in 3 weeks; FinBank will not accept any behavior that could result in cross-region serving.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Product Manager, Inference Control
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finbank_requirement_matrix.pdf (application/pdf), proposed-routing-policy.yaml (text/yaml)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Customer ask: FinBank requires strict routing

Lauren,

Thanks for the context and the YAML. From an infra standpoint:
- Region lock is straightforward at the routing layer (we can bind a tenant to a region tag).
- Preventing cross-region fallback is also doable, but it carries availability trade-offs — if eu-west runs out of capacity requests will start failing. We need a clear SLA carve-out and customer acknowledgment of availability risk.
- For exact model-hash pinning, we need to ensure artifact immutability and storage residency (model blob must be available within eu-west). Replicating large models into region-specific object stores will add provisioning time.

Questions:
1) How large are the models FinBank will request? (Llama-2-70B/Redwood-Large/Custom?)
2) Do they expect cold-starts to succeed immediately or accept delayed availability during provisioning?
3) Can we require a lead time (e.g., 48–72 hours) for model pin provisioning?

I'll run capacity modelling once I know model size and expected RPS.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finbank.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@acmelegal.com
Date: 2026-07-19T13:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Customer ask: FinBank requires strict routing

Lauren / team,

Thanks — a couple clarifications from our security/compliance team: we will not accept any automatic fallback that results in serving from non-EU regions. If the requested model is unavailable we prefer an explicit failure. We also expect a log stream that proves inference execution and region of execution for audit (we'll want to map that into our internal SIEM).

Model sizes: initially planning to use Redwood-13B and a tuned 33B variant for higher-risk endpoints. No immediate plans for 70B, but we reserve the right to request it later.

Provisioning: 48 hours lead time is acceptable. Regarding exact artifact pinning: the model repository URL and model hash will be supplied before provisioning.

Regulatory note: any model weights or telemetry must remain in EU physical locations.

Marcus Lee
Head of Platform Security
FinBank
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T15:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Customer ask: FinBank requires strict routing

Looping in ops questions and risk notes.

Operational impact:
- No-fallback policies will increase error rates during peak or infra incidents. We need to define a clear incident playbook for the FinBank tenant (alerting thresholds, who gets paged, runbook steps).
- We should add an explicit customer opt-in checkbox in the Console that documents they accept degraded availability in exchange for strict routing. That will help with support and billing disputes.

Security/Telemetry:
- We'll add a log export to a dedicated EU-only S3 bucket (KMS-encrypted) and provide a signed link for FinBank to pull into their SIEM. Audit trail will include node id, region, model hash, timestamp, and request-id.

Next actions I propose:
1) Product to finalize the policy text and Console UX for opt-in.
2) Infra to produce a capacity / provisioning plan for 13B and 33B variants with estimated lead times and cost delta.
3) Legal to draft contract language to record the availability carve-out and data residency guarantees.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Production Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-20T08:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Customer ask: FinBank requires strict routing

Thanks everyone for the quick input. A few product notes and proposed wording for the customer contract and Console:

Product/Console proposal (draft):
- Tenant-level toggle: "Enforce region-only routing (EU-west) — disallow automatic cross-region fallback" (default: off).
- Model pinning: "Lock model by artifact hash: requests will be served only by the exact model artifact specified" with a warning modal explaining provisioning lead time and availability risks.
- Visibility: Provide per-tenant metrics showing failed requests due to policy (HTTP 503 policy-block).

Contract wording snippet (for Legal):
"Customer acknowledges and accepts that choosing 'Enforce region-only routing' may result in requests failing when capacity in the specified region is unavailable. Redwood will not automatically route traffic to other regions or model variants if this option is selected. Redwood will provide a provisioning lead time of 48–72 hours for new model artifact pins."

Action items assigned:
- Jonas: capacity plan for 13B + 33B (due 2026-07-22)
- Hannah: ops runbook and log-export design (due 2026-07-23)
- Legal (cc contracts@acmelegal.com): draft contract language and SLA carve-out (due 2026-07-24)
- Karthik: communicate pilot timeline to FinBank and confirm they accept the Console opt-in flow (due 2026-07-21)

I'll slot this as a priority product ask and prepare the Console mocks once Legal confirms wording.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus.Lee@finbank.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@acmelegal.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-20T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Customer ask: FinBank requires strict routing

Marcus,

Appreciate the clarity. We'll proceed with the pilot under the conditions outlined by Rishi and the team. Quick confirmations from our side:
- FinBank will provide the model hash and repo link at least 72 hours before the scheduled pilot start for provisioning.
- FinBank accepts the availability carve-out and will treat policy-blocked failures as part of the agreed behavior for the pilot.

I'll update the HubSpot deal with these notes and attach the requirement matrix and routing YAML. Expect a follow-up calendar invite for the pilot kickoff on 2026-07-25.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
